status: Comparison envelopes are UNAPPROVED decision-support scenarios. The selected_plan total and objective are group choices (D-032); its line items and every performance assumption remain agent proposals, not Green SM budgets, forecasts or agreed KPI targets

selected_plan.segment: S1 resident self-paid repeat taxi users
selected_plan.positioning: P1 clear local taxi choice, with a route to resolution
selected_plan.objective: Market entry: awareness and trial among S1, with repeat use as the scale gate
selected_plan.line_items: Agent proposal for group approval: the middle envelope with account/partner sales removed; its 90 hours move to CRM/support (+60) and local content/creative (+30); media, DOOH, tools, incentive reserve and contingency unchanged. No conversion credit is given for the moved hours

cost_basis: Media list costs exclude VAT and production; production is separately budgeted. Other inputs are planning allowances on the same provisional net-of-recoverable-VAT basis. Actual tax treatment and supplier quotes require validation.

dooh_cpm.scope: 2026 Digital Copenhagen DOOH list CPM, 41 screens; not Meta CPM or unique people

dooh_setup.scope: Published setup per assumed single campaign, includes five creative variants; actual minimum order and campaign configuration unconfirmed

fare_start.scope: Published Day (Min) meter schedule; not app maximum or actual average fare

common_assumptions.note: Every field in common_assumptions is an agent planning choice, not observed company or market performance. The trip is a standardised calculation, not an average journey. Paid acquisition and B2B accounts must be de-duplicated at rider/booking level; model assumes disjoint attributed ride groups. No incremental DOOH conversions are invented.

performance_warning: These are deliberately transparent stress assumptions, not published benchmarks, probabilistic intervals, empirical estimates or forecast confidence bounds. Conversion assumptions do not depend on every acquired rider receiving a voucher; voucher redemption is capped by the reserve. Changing spend does not establish scalable linear returns.
